mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen modestly across the last four weeks (9.9 -> 13.0 -> 11.7), indicating increased time spent at home that structurally suppresses discretionary retail trips; this persistent elevation predicts continued suppression of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 10 for all four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week TRANSIT decline exceeding 5 points signals renewed mobility restrictions such as curfews or capacity limits, which will further depress retail footfall within the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped from -34.7 to -40.4 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline (direction_4w = '+') within two weeks after a TRANSIT week-on-week drop exceeding 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: When both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility decline in the same week, this signals compounded restriction of work-related and transit-based movement that cross-reinforces reduced discretionary shopping trips, producing a larger negative shift in RETAIL_REC than either series would predict alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both decline in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT declined together between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises despite simultaneous weekly declines in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As the decision date in mid-November approaches the holiday shopping season, consumer urgency to complete in-person pre-holiday purchases will push RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks despite recent suppression, overriding short-term mobility restriction signals.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2020-11-15, within weeks of the major holiday shopping period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days remains below or equal to the last 28-day mean despite the approaching holiday season.

mechanism_narrative: A single-week rebound in PARKS mobility exceeding 15 points signals a temporary good-weather or event-driven outdoor activity surge that substitutes for indoor retail visits, producing a short-term dip in RETAIL_REC the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -33.1 to -12.1 between t-3w and t-2w, a 21-point increase
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week following a PARKS week-on-week rise exceeding 15 points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained comparatively stable and far less negative than RETAIL_REC across all four weeks, indicating essential-trip behavior is decoupled from discretionary retail; continued stability in GROCERY_PHARM predicts no strong reversal in RETAIL_REC's current negative trend over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises significantly (direction_4w = '+') while GROCERY_PHARM remains flat, invalidating the decoupling assumption.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in WORKPLACES and rise in RESIDENTIAL within the same week indicates households are complying with new stay-at-home guidance, and this joint signal predicts an immediate one-week drop in RETAIL_REC larger than either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES declines and RESIDENTIAL rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -26.9 to -34.0 while RESIDENTIAL rose from 9.9 to 13.0 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week after WORKPLACES declines and RESIDENTIAL rises together.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT stabilizes within a narrow band of less than 3 points week-on-week change over two consecutive weeks, it signals a plateau in mobility restrictions consistent with seasonal routine adaptation, after which RETAIL_REC will stabilize and modestly recover over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change stays within +/-3 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT changed by only 1.7 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline despite TRANSIT stabilizing within a narrow band for two weeks.
